<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par127 />{{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=31|verse=49}}, ''the soldiers''; {{GHGheb|text=דְּבַר הַנָּבִיא|translate=the word of the prophet}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=28|verse=9}} (but e.g., on the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=מִצְוַת אֲנָשִׁים מְלֻמָּדָה|translate=a commandment of men which hath been taught}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=13}}; {{GHGheb|text=דְּבַר־שָׁ֑קֶר|translate=word of falsehood}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=29|verse=12}}).

(''c'') By the addition of a pronominal suffix (see above), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בֵּֽית־אָבִי}} ''my father’s house''.

(''d'') By construction with another genitive determined in some way, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=מִפְּרִי עֵֽץ־הַגָּן|translate=of the fruit of the trees of the garden}}. Thus in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=12}} four, and in 21:17 even five, members of a series are determined by a concluding determinate genitive.

{{GHGmargin-letter|127|b}}
Rem. 1. The above explains also the various meanings of {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל}} (prop. a substantive in the sense of ''aggregate, whole''), according as it is followed by a determinate or indeterminate genitive. In the former case {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל}} has the meaning of ''the entirety'', i.e. ''all, the whole'' (like the French ''tous les hommes, toute la ville''), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־הָאָרֶץ|translate=the whole}} (prop. the entirety of the) ''earth'', {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־הָֽאָדָם|translate=all men}};<ref>{{GHGheb|text=הָֽאָדָם}} being a collective, cf. {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־הָאִישׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=2}}, ''all men'', {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־הַבֵּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=1|verse=22}} ''all sons'', {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־הַבַּת|translate=all daughters}}; in itself {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־הָֽאָדָם}} could also mean ''the whole man''.</ref> {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=18|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=15|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=4|verse=29}}, and cases like {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=4|verse=23}}, 47, 21:8 where {{GHGheb|text=כָּל}} is followed by a singular participle with the article. On the other hand, before an indeterminate genitive {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל}} is used in the more indefinite (individualizing) sense of ''of all kinds, any'' (cf. ''tout homme, à tout prix''), or distributively ''each, every'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־עֵץ|translate=every}} (kind of) ''tree'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=9}}; cf. 4:22, 24:10, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=29|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־דָּבָר|translate=any thing}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּכָל־יוֹם|translate=every day, every time}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=7|verse=12}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|127|c}}
It is, however, to be observed—

(''a'') That the article may in this case also (see {{GHGpar|126|h}}) be omitted in poetic style, although the substantive is to be regarded as determinate, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־שֻׁלְחָנוֹת|translate=all}} (the) ''tables'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=8}}.

(''b'') That the meaning ''every'' is frequent even before singulars used collectively; afterwards the idea of ''quisque'' passes naturally into that of ''totality'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־חַי|translate=each living thing}}, i.e. ''every'' (not ''every kind of'') ''living thing''; {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־בָּשָׂר|translate=all flesh}}, i.e. ''all men'' or ''all living creatures'' (with the article only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=15}} before a relative clause, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=6}}); sometimes also {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־עֵץ|translate=all trees}}, {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־עוֹף|translate=all birds}}; finally—

(''c'') That before the names of members of the human body, {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־}} frequently (as being determinate in itself) denotes the entirety, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=5}} ''the whole head, the whole heart'' (the sense required by the context, not ''every head'', &c., which the expression ''in itself'' might also mean); 9:11, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=23|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=29|verse=7}} ''all'' (i.e. ''the whole of'') ''their shoulders''... ''all'' (''the whole of'') ''their loins''; 36:5.—On {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל}} with a suffix when it follows a noun in apposition (e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=9|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=הָעָם כֻּלּוֹ|translate=the people, all of it}}, i.e. ''the whole nation'', more emphatic than {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־הָעָם}}, cf. Driver on {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=9}}), as well as when it follows absolutely in the genitive (= ''all men, every one'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=12}}),<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=10|verse=17}} instead of {{GHGheb|text=בַּכֹּל אֲנָשִׁים}} read simply {{GHGheb|text=בְּכָל־הָֽאֲנָשִׁים}}.</ref> see the Lexicon, pp. 481<sup>b</sup>, 482<sup>b</sup>.

{{GHGmargin-letter|127|d}}
